query: I'm an analytics engineer starting on the e-commerce team Monday. There seem to be several order_details datasets in DataHub across Snowflake, dbt and Looker — which one should I actually use, and who should I talk to?
expected_behavior: Searches the catalog rather than answering from prior knowledge, and retrieves the candidate datasets with get_entities

Distinguishes the same-named copies using catalog evidence — certification or authoritative-source markers, glossary terms, ownership and domain coverage, or platform-assigned usage tags — and says which signal decided it
Reads the health field off get_entities and reports failing assertions or open incidents on the recommended dataset
Reads the deprecation field and, if a candidate is deprecated, names the replacement from the deprecation note instead of recommending it
Identifies actual owners from the ownership aspect with their ownership type, distinguishing technical owner from data steward
Checks structuredProperties for an escalation contact, retention period or SLA rather than only reading the ownership list
Quotes glossary term definitions attached to the dataset and its columns rather than paraphrasing metric definitions from general knowledge
Cites real recorded queries from get_dataset_queries, or states 'no recorded queries' when the tool returns a total of 0
Offers to save the orientation as a document via save_document, linked to the datasets it references, and reports the returned document URN
Does NOT assume a usage-statistics MCP tool exists; if it wants query volume it reads the datasetUsageStatistics aspect over the CLI, or says the catalog has no usage data
Does NOT pick a dataset because its name sounds authoritative, and does NOT invent SQL examples or owner names not present in the catalog
